processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent ST condition (proc_st-1050c-1h-wq) from which the 650-6 sample was subsequently aged.
Aging of solution-treated samples at 650 °C for 6 h (designated 650-6). Intragranular κ-carbides coarsen to ≈24 nm, accompanied by more pronounced intergranular κ-carbide precipitation.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix with nanoscale intragranular κ-carbides (≈24 nm) and more pronounced intergranular κ-carbide precipitation at grain boundaries.

microstructure_list.region: austenite grain interiors and grain boundaries

phases_present.morphology: coarse precipitates decorating grain boundaries; more pronounced than in 550-6/600-6

precipitates.distribution: at grain boundaries; more pronounced precipitation

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Repeated dislocation shearing disrupts the ordered κ structure and forms anti-phase boundaries/shear steps, consistent with mechanical dissolution of κ-carbides during cyclic loading.
Coarse intergranular κ precipitates act as strong slip barriers, intensify dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentration, leading to earlier crack nucleation and shortened fatigue life.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation slip through glide-plane softening; intragranular κ enhances slip reversibility, but intergranular κ impedes slip transmission across grain boundaries.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Intragranular κ-carbides undergo mechanical dissolution via repeated dislocation shearing during cyclic loading.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone, gauge 5 mm wide × 2.5 mm thick, 15 mm gauge section; tensile axis parallel to rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Shimadzu AG-Xplus 250 kN universal testing machine; surfaces mechanically polished and electropolished.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: 650-6 (blue) yields between 600 and 700 MPa, peaks between 900 and 1000 MPa, then drops abruptly, terminating near 52–53% strain.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone (same dimensions as tensile samples); loading axis parallel to rolling direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Stress-controlled tension–tension fatigue; sinusoidal waveform; frequency 20 Hz; stress ratio R = 0.1; Shimadzu EHF-EV050K2A-020-1 servo-hydraulic machine. Basquin fit parameters for 650-6: σ'_f = 1153, b = -0.12, RMSE(log10 Nf) = 0.1139.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Fatigue strength (max stress amplitude for 10^7 cycles): 650-6 = 171 MPa vs 600-6 = 175.5 MPa (650-6 second-best among aged samples at low stress amplitudes); at high stress amplitudes 650-6 shows the poorest fatigue life among aged samples.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM foils ~50 μm thick, twin-jet electropolishing in 8 vol.% perchloric acid in ethanol at 30 V, electrolyte ~ -20 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize κ-carbide precipitation in aged samples (550-6, 600-6, 650-6)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Intragranular κ-carbides ≈24 nm and more pronounced intergranular κ precipitation at grain boundaries in the 650-6 sample.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: post-fractured fracture surfaces and lateral surfaces; stress amplitudes 180 MPa and 315 MPa
characterization_methods.purpose: Fracture surface morphology and crack-propagation zone characterization
characterization_methods.key_findings: fΔ (crack initiation+propagation zone area fraction) = 0.63 at 180 MPa and 0.32 at 315 MPa; fatigue striations present but coarser/less regular than in 550-6/600-6; rapid fracture zone shows mixed dimple + cleavage-facet morphology, indicating reduced ductility.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD on SEM, step size 0.8 μm; AZtecCrystal post-processing software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: adjacent to main fatigue cracks; stress amplitude 225 MPa
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze crack propagation path and local strain fields
characterization_methods.key_findings: Crack propagates transgranularly along slip bands with greater tortuosity and microbranching vs ST; localized KAM hot spots at grain boundaries decorated with intergranular κ-carbides indicate intense local strain concentration, consistent with reduced fatigue life.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: post-fractured samples; foils extracted from gauge sections; Δσ/2 = 180 MPa and 315 MPa
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize deformation microstructures and dislocation–carbide interactions
characterization_methods.key_findings: Planar slip bands with lower overall dislocation density than ST; intragranular κ (~24 nm) remains in shearing regime; HRTEM/IFFT shows shear steps and localized contrast (APBs) consistent with mechanical dissolution of κ under cyclic loading; near grain boundaries, coarse intergranular κ blocks slip and produces dislocation pile-ups.

analytical_models.equation_role: Interpret κ-carbide strengthening contributions: coherency strain strengthening Δσ_cs, modulus mismatch strengthening Δσ_ms, and order strengthening Δσ_os.
analytical_models.model_note: For 650-6, intragranular κ-carbides (~24 nm) remain in the shearing regime; Δσ_cs and Δσ_ms increase with precipitate size at fixed f, but severe intergranular precipitation offsets the intragranular benefit.

unmapped_findings: The reduced tensile strength of the 650-6 sample (YS 579 ± 14 MPa; UTS 978 ± 4 MPa) is attributed to grain boundary weakening caused by serious intergranular κ-carbide precipitation (b0026).

At high stress amplitudes, the 650-6 sample shows the poorest fatigue life among the aged samples (ranking: 550-6 best, 600-6 intermediate, 650-6 poorest), tracking the increasing severity of intergranular precipitation (b0080).
